summary: Send request bodies whose parameter names use Rails bracket convention as application/x-www-form-urlencoded instead of application/json, so Canvas actually sees them. Every write command in the CLI and MCP server was silently no-opping with HTTP 200.
reason:
The generated command tree builds request bodies as a flat map keyed by the parameter names straight out of the Canvas API docs, which are Rails bracket names: body["wiki_page[body]"], body["assignment[name]"], body["course_ids[]"]. internal/client/client.go then json.Marshal'd that map and sent it as application/json. Canvas is a Rails app, and Rails only expands bracket names into a nested params hash when they arrive as a query string or a form-encoded body -- that expansion is Rack's parse_nested_query. A JSON body is handed to JSON.parse and merged into params verbatim, with no bracket expansion, so {"wiki_page[body]": "x"} lands under the literal key "wiki_page[body]" and params[:wiki_page] stays nil.

The failure mode was silent, which is why it went unnoticed: Canvas answered PUT /courses/87/pages/<url> with HTTP 200 and the unmodified page, so the CLI reported success and printed a page object while nothing had changed. Only endpoints with a required attribute surfaced anything at all, and then misleadingly -- `pages create` returned 400 "Title can't be blank" while a title was plainly being sent.

Blast radius was the whole write surface: 1,042 bracketed body keys across 155 files in internal/cli, spanning 87 distinct parameter prefixes (account, assignment, course, enrollment, submission, quiz, ...), plus the same surface re-exposed as MCP tools. Fixing it at the 1,042 call sites would not survive a reprint and would fight the generator, so the encoding decision is made once at the single client chokepoint where the body is serialized.

Only top-level keys are inspected for a bracket. A body handed in through --stdin as genuine nested JSON ({"wiki_page":{"body":"x"}}) has no bracketed key, stays on the JSON path, and keeps working -- Canvas accepts that form too, and it was the only way to write through this CLI before the fix.

Upstream: the generator should decide body encoding from the parameter-name convention of the spec it is printing, rather than defaulting every body to JSON. A Rails-style API described with bracket parameter names cannot be driven with a JSON body.
known_limitations:
Coverage: of 537 distinct bracketed keys across 1,051 occurrences, 512 distinct (989 occurrences, 94%) conform to Rack's parse_nested_query grammar and are carried correctly by this patch. The remaining 25 distinct keys (62 occurrences) are malformed independently of it and are NOT addressed -- they were broken under JSON encoding too, and form encoding neither fixes nor regresses them. Four families:

1. Unsubstituted doc placeholders baked into the key -- 16 keys, 49 occurrences, in submissions_bulk_update{,_2,_3,_4}.go, external_tools_create{,_2}.go, roles_add_role.go, roles_update.go, notification_preferences_update_all{,_2}.go. Example: body["grade_data[<student_id>][posted_grade]"]. This is the worst of the four: the generated flag surface offers --grade-data-student-id-posted-grade but no flag to say WHICH student, so the literal string <student_id> ships in the key and the command is unusable through flags no matter how the body is encoded. The generator needs to emit a map-valued flag (or repeatable key=value pairs) for endpoints whose params are keyed by a caller-supplied id.

2. Leading-bracket names -- 7 keys, in lti_contextcontrols_post_bulk.go and lti_resource_links_post_bulk.go. Example: body["[]account_id"]. These endpoints take a bare JSON array as the request body; the generator flattened the array element's fields into top-level keys prefixed with [], which is not a thing in any encoding.

3. Literal wildcard -- 1 key, 5 occurrences, in content_migrations_create{,_2,_3,_4}.go and sis_imports_create.go: body["pre_attachment[*]"]. The '*' is documentation notation for 'any pre_attachment sub-field', not a parameter name.

4. Nested bracket inside a subscript -- 1 key, in course_reports_create.go: body["parameters[section_ids[]]"]. The documented parameter is almost certainly parameters[section_ids][]; the generator mis-nested the list marker.

Workaround for all four: --stdin accepts a genuine JSON document, which has no bracketed top-level key, stays on the JSON path, and is accepted by Canvas -- including a top-level JSON array, which is exactly what family 2 needs.

Separately, and unrelated to encoding: the client has no multipart implementation at all, so the --attachment flags on discussion_topics_create{,_2}.go, discussion_topics_add_entry{,_2}.go and discussion_topics_add_reply.go send a plain string rather than a file. File upload has never worked and is out of scope here.
validated_outcome: Root cause reproduced and fixed against a live Canvas instance. Before: PUT with {"wiki_page[body]": "..."} as JSON returned HTTP 200 with the page body unchanged; POST /pages returned 400 "Title can't be blank" despite sending a title. After: the same CLI invocations change the page and create it correctly. Controls confirmed the diagnosis -- nested JSON ({"wiki_page":{"body":...}}) and form-encoded (wiki_page[body]=...) both wrote successfully where flat-bracketed JSON did not. Unit tests cover the bracket shapes the tree actually emits (parent[child], list[], list[][field], deep nesting, bool/number rendering, nil omission, reserved-character escaping) and assert non-bracketed bodies still go out as application/json. One encoder bug was caught by those tests before shipping: keys already containing an empty bracket pair must repeat as-is rather than gain a second []. Full Go suite passes; --dry-run now prints the form body and its Content-Type instead of printing nothing.
